title: Oct 10 Results + Oct 11 Preview: Perfect on a Short Slate
summary: Clean sweep on Oct 10 with Guardians. Tomorrow: Brewers host Dodgers in a spicy matchup.

content.value:
## October 10: One Swing, One Hit

You know what I love about the playoffs? Short slates. One game, one call, and we nailed it. The Guardians took care of business at home against the Sox, and our 53% lean turned into a clean checkmark. Nothing fancy, just solid postseason baseball the way it's supposed to be played in Cleveland.

## The Guardians Formula

I've seen this story before. Home playoff game, crowd energized, steady pitching, and timely hitting. The Guardians didn't need to reinvent the wheel here—they just played their brand of October baseball. The 53% probability reflected what we all knew: this was a coin flip with home-field advantage as the deciding factor.

In the playoffs, that's often all you need.

## October 11: Now This Gets Interesting

Tomorrow we've got a matchup that makes you lean back in your chair and think for a minute. The Dodgers head to Milwaukee, and we're looking at a pitcher's duel that has all the makings of a classic postseason chess match.

## The Brewers Lean: 61% Confidence

Here's what caught my eye: we're giving Milwaukee a 61% edge at home despite Tarik Skubal taking the ball for Los Angeles. Now, Skubal's no slouch—the guy's been one of the best arms in baseball when healthy. But Jacob Misiorowski on the bump for the Brewers in front of that Milwaukee crowd? 

I've seen enough playoff series to know that home mound advantage with a talented young arm can be the difference. The Brewers have been playing with house money all season, and American Family Field in October is a different animal.

This isn't a slam dunk—61% never is—but it's a solid lean backed by the factors that matter in playoff baseball: starting pitching, home crowd energy, and a team that believes it belongs here.

## The Skubal Factor

Let's not pretend Skubal doesn't make this interesting. When he's on, he's electric. The Dodgers didn't hand him the ball in a playoff game by accident. This is the kind of game that comes down to which starter blinks first, which bullpen holds, and which lineup scratches across that one big inning.

But Milwaukee at home, with Misiorowski's stuff playing up in October? I'll take that 61% and feel good about it.

## The Bottom Line

We went 1-0 yesterday because we trusted the process and didn't overthink a short slate. Tomorrow, we're doing the same thing. The Brewers have the edge—not a massive one, but enough to make them the pick.

That's playoff baseball. You make the call, you trust your read, and you live with the results. See you after first pitch.

—Max
